subject: Regionally muted responses — Hosted API incident notification (Jan 27)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@meridianhealth.com>, eng@meridianhealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 27 Jan 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Regionally muted responses — Hosted API incident notification (Jan 27)

Hi Ava / Meridian team,

We detected a partial degradation affecting responses routed through our US-WEST-2 serving pool this morning between ~07:50–08:05 PST. Symptoms included: intermittent empty/truncated responses for streaming calls, elevated 5xx rates (peaked ~2% of requests for affected tenants), and higher P99 latencies for a subset of generation requests.

What we did immediately:
- Diversion: shifted new requests away from the affected sub-pool and increased capacity in nearby pools.
- Flush: issued a controlled KV-cache flush for the variant family experiencing early-termination behaviors.
- Retry guidance: advised short exponential retries; pinning to us-east variants temporarily avoids the issue.

Impact to Meridian: our telemetry shows ~0.6% of Meridian requests during the window returned truncated streams; no data exposure. We consider this a partial service degradation for certain streaming workloads.

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (short event log).

We are actively investigating the root cause and will provide an update within 60 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we know reliability is critical and we're prioritizing a full remediation and clear next steps.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 27 Jan 2027 09:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Regionally muted responses — initial engineering observations

Grace / team,

Quick internal update — early signs point to a confluence of two factors: (1) a recently deployed kernel optimization for the 8-bit quantized variant that falls back to a different attention path under certain sequence-length distributions, and (2) a KV-cache eviction storm triggered by an autoscaler race when nodes were rebalanced. The fallback path has a regression where the streaming loop terminates prematurely on some token emission paths.

Mitigations applied at 08:03 PST:
- We rolled back the kernel optimization on the affected worker group.
- Increased the warm pool size to prevent immediate evictions.
- Enabled secondary routing so traffic for pinned Meridian users went to stable variants in us-east.

Next steps: full trace-level collection and timeline reconstruction (I have a ticket open). If the rollback holds for 1 hour with drop in error/termination rates, we'll schedule a controlled re-deploy with additional guardrails.

Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — Jan 27 US-WEST-2 partial degradation

Hi Ava / Meridian team,

Thank you for your patience while we completed our investigation. Attached is the formal postmortem (hosted_inference_postmortem-20270129.pdf) and a CSV timeline (incident_timeline.csv). Summary below:

Incident summary:
- Window: 2027-01-27 07:50–08:05 PST (root cause window)
- Impact: Partial degradation for streaming generation traffic routed to US-WEST-2; ~0.6% of Meridian requests experienced truncated/early-terminated streams. No user data was exposed.
- Root cause: An interaction between a newly deployed 8-bit kernel optimization and a KV-cache eviction surge during autoscaler rebalancing caused an edge-case in the streaming loop that prematurely terminated emission for certain token sequences.

Remediation and long-term fixes:
- Immediate: rollback of the kernel optimization in the affected pool and adjusted autoscaler cooldowns (complete 08:03 PST).
- Short-term: additional validation checks added to the rollout pipeline to detect streaming termination regressions; expanded tracing on streaming paths.
- Long-term: safer staged rollout strategy for kernel changes, circuit-breaker that prevents eviction storms from coinciding with kernel deploys, and a firmware/gemm-kernel patch scheduled for Q1 to eliminate the fallback regression.

Compensation: We will review SLA impact and follow up with a formal credit offer if the incident meets your contract threshold. I will loop in your account rep separately with proposed credit terms.

Attachments: hosted_inference_postmortem-20270129.pdf (detailed RCA and timeline), incident-runbook.pdf (runbook updates). Also: incident timeline available at https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-01-27-region-muted-responses.

If you prefer continued short-term mitigation, pinning to us-east variants is an accepted stable workaround; our solutions engineer can assist with a scoped traffic policy.

Please let us know any additional questions or if you'd like a follow-up call.

— Grace
